correctness.rationale: From the strict rJR criterion 2*h_c*|N(c) intersect U(W)|<n, failure of a maximum-quality pair {a,b} gives a third candidate c with at least n/(2h_c) uncovered supporters. Since s<=n-d, h_c>=n/[2(n-d)]. Replacing b with c covers s+d>n/2 and is rJR; the ratio is >=(1+n/[2(n-d)])/2. At 2d=n the repair has identical maximum quality; when 2d>n no maximum pair can fail. The sharp example with disjoint T,S, supports T,T,S and qualities 1,1,n/[2(n-d)] attains the ratio. Integer boundaries and strict tie handled. Independent integer-grid enumeration covers 630342 3-candidate cases for n=4,5, not an all-instance proof.
